bk3-1a: The tripper pays nothing for the jug: a person has no right to leave his things in the public domain (Mishnah 3:1; Kulp).
The owner pays for the injury (Mishnah 3:1).
bk3-1b: The owner of a jug that breaks in the public domain is liable for those who slip on the water or are cut by the shards (Mishnah 3:1; Rabbi Judah adds the question of intention).
bk3-2a: Pouring water into the public domain makes him liable for the injury (Mishnah 3:2).
bk3-2b: A thorn fence that falls into the public domain makes its owner liable for the injury (Mishnah 3:2).
bk3-3: Whoever puts straw out in the public domain is liable for the injury, and whoever comes first may take it (Mishnah 3:3).
bk3-4: The first pot-seller is liable for the injury to the second, if he could have got up in time (Mishnah 3:4; Kehati).
bk3-5s: Each has the right to walk in the public domain, so the beam owner is exempt (Mishnah 3:5).
bk3-5a: The beam owner in front is exempt: the jar owner walked into him (Mishnah 3:5).
bk3-5b: If the beam owner stops suddenly without warning, he is liable (Mishnah 3:5).
bk3-5c: If the beam owner warns the other to stop, he is exempt (Mishnah 3:5).
bk3-6: Neither pays: two people in the public domain, one running and one walking, or both running, who injure each other are both exempt (Mishnah 3:6).
Neither pays: two people in the public domain, one running and one walking, or both running, who injure each other are both exempt (Mishnah 3:6).
bk3-7: One who splits wood is liable for the injury wherever he works and wherever the damage is (Mishnah 3:7).
bk3-11a: The one who wants payment must bring the proof (hamotzi mechavero alav hara'ayah): each owner blames the other, so both are exempt (Mishnah 3:11).
The one who wants payment must bring the proof (hamotzi mechavero alav hara'ayah): each owner blames the other, so both are exempt (Mishnah 3:11).
bk3-11b: When both oxen have one owner there is no one else to blame, so he is liable (Mishnah 3:11).
bk5-1: A harmless ox pays half damages for the cow (Mishnah 5:1).

When it is in doubt whether the goring caused the loss, the mishnah has them split the doubtful amount: half of the half, a quarter. This follows Sumchus; the halakha follows the Sages, that nothing is paid unless proven (Kehati).
